Resolves #19800

A sort by a property named `index` emptied the collection. `Collection#doSort` sorts through a map that remembered each item's position as `index`, and `Sorter#useTransformValue` defaults to true, so every property sort took that path. A sort property of the same name overwrote the position, and the map back looked items up by field value. The position now lives under a Symbol, `sortPosition`, declared beside the module's other Symbols.

Evidence: L2 (a unit spec red on `dev`, the full unit suite, a live drive of the covid grid) → L2 required (AC-1–AC-4).

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `SortByIndexField.spec.mjs`, "a Collection keeps every item and orders them by index…": ASC, DESC and `index` as the second of two sorters. On `dev` it fails with wrong items and `undefined` entries. |
| AC-2 | Same spec, "a Store sorting raw items by an index field keeps every item": `count` 5 and the expected order. Red on `dev`. |
| AC-3 | Live on `examples/grid/covid` at `e70b86fd6a`: the `#` header, then Cases, keeps every row (USA, India, France on top). On `dev`, the first click emptied the grid with TypeErrors on `country`, `colspan`, `cases` and `annotations.selected`. |
| AC-4 | `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/collection test/playwright/unit/data`: 310 passed. The full unit suite: 5,226 passed, with one known local failure (below). |
